Yes — NovaLearn should fund the Advanced OCR work before accelerating the Teams integration.

- **Current support demand:** Scanned PDF processing is the primary driver of citation errors and customer onboarding delays, and the Advanced OCR Pipeline is the highest technical priority to resolve these issues [NL-001]. In May 2026, 27% of support tickets were related to import issues and broken citations from scanned PDFs, clogging the support queue [NL-015]. This is a system stability requirement, not a nice-to-have [NL-015].
- **Onboarding impact:** Scanned PDF ingestion, alongside permission mapping, remains NovaLearn’s primary onboarding bottleneck [NL-016]. Fixing ingestion and citation accuracy must come before delivering answers through a new channel; otherwise, the platform would deliver inaccurate, un-cited answers to a larger audience inside Teams [NL-015].
- **Roadmap status:** The OCR Pipeline is scheduled for August 2026 [NL-001][NL-015]. The Teams integration is still in the design phase for Q4 2026, with development slated for early 2027 [NL-015][NL-014]. The roadmap is a planning document and timelines are not contractual commitments [NL-014], but accelerating Teams would require a complete redesign of the auth layer to enforce role-based access control and tenant isolation — rushing it risks a tenant-isolation breach [NL-015]. The approved position is that Teams will be designed from the ground up to enforce active user permissions [NL-032].
- **Conclusion:** Prioritizing OCR first addresses the current support load and onboarding bottleneck, while Teams acceleration should not displace that work [NL-001][NL-015]. The Teams integration is high demand [NL-011], but the evidence indicates it is not ready and should follow the existing Q4 design timeline [NL-014][NL-015].
